messages.content:
Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: Overall, vitamin D concentrations in late pregnancy were not associated with risk of postpartum depression.
Sentence: "Overall, we found no association between vitamin D concentrations and risk of PPD (p = 0.08)."
Measured as: postpartum depression (PPD)
Population: Women in the Danish National Birth Cohort: 605 with postpartum depression and 875 controls
Intervention: Late pregnancy serum 25[OH]D3 concentration (measured, not given)
Comparator: Women with vitamin D concentrations of 50-79 nmol/L
Design: case-control study
Sample size: 1,480
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Women from minority ethnic groups were less likely than white British women to be diagnosed with depression in primary care.
Sentence: "Women from minority ethnic groups were less likely to be diagnosed with depression in primary care compared with white British women (adjusted OR 0.66 (0.55-0.79) p<0.001), and black women were more likely to have a SMI (adjusted OR 2.79 (2.13-3.64) p<0.001)."
Measured as: diagnosis of depression in primary care
Population: Women aged 15-40 in contact with secondary mental health services and age-matched comparison women, Lambeth, London
Intervention: No intervention; exposure is minority ethnicity (not vitamin D)
Comparator: White British women
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 18,349
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"rationale":"Study B's exposure is minority ethnicity, not vitamin D, so it does not bear on the vitamin D question.","verdict":"off_question","reason":null,"also_differs":[],"detail":"exposure: minority ethnicity vs white British, not vitamin D"}
